clue.text: Game flirt getting run in

indicators.note: in tells us the run is placed inside the word for a flirt

parts.note: a coquet is an old word for a flirt, a person who toys with admirers
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A flirtatious player sneaks a run into a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; 'in' puts R inside COQUET. CROQUET is the lawn game played with mallets and hoops.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn sport where balls are struck through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: Dumbo? He needed dress

parts.note: a dumbo is a fool, and so is a clot in British slang

explanation.surface: Dumbo the elephant needed something to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a link. 'Dumbo' suggests the elephant, but it is a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe someone is to dress them in garments.

clue.text: Enclosure not right in airport for all to see

indicators.note: in means the enclosure goes inside the trimmed airport name
not right means the abbreviation R for right is removed

parts.note: Orly is one of the airports serving Paris
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: An animal pen that isn't right is in an airport where everyone can see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' drops R from the Paris airport, and 'in' puts the enclosure inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly means doing it publicly, in plain view of everyone.

clue.text: Risk exam failure as reserve player?

definitions.meaning: to study too little, read as ..., is to risk failing an exam
a stand-in actor who learns a role in case the lead cannot perform

explanation.surface: Someone risks failing an exam and ends up only a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. The first definition treats the answer as a verb, under-study, meaning not do enough revision.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy is an actor ready to take a role if the regular performer is absent.

clue.text: Historian no American understood

indicators.note: no means the American abbreviation is to be left out

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A historian who was not American was well understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes US off the end of TACITUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied without being stated, so understood.

clue.text: Youngster in form

parts.note: a form is the shallow lair where a hare lies, so the young creature found there is a baby hare

explanation.surface: A young person who is on good form, or in a school form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' suggests a school class or fitness; it is the hollow in grass where a hare rests.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare is the youngster that lies in a form, the hare's resting hollow.

clue.text: Rake it in with rebel in a state

indicators.note: in a state means agitated or disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A womaniser takes his cut alongside a rebel in some American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' rearranges IT IN and REBEL; 'with' is a link. 'Rake' looks like a garden tool or verb, but it is a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker, a libertine.

clue.text: … that's extremely loathsome and obnoxious

parts.note: the ellipsis stands in place of the clue's own number, six, written in Roman numerals

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of the word loathsome

explanation.surface: Something is supremely loathsome and offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens on its own number: read '6 that's extremely loathsome', with 6 as VI in Roman numerals. 'extremely' takes the end letters of 'loathsome'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vile means thoroughly unpleasant, so obnoxious.

clue.text: Writer presenting murder victim in lift? Not quite

indicators.note: in means the victim's name goes inside the shortened word
not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to lift is to raise
in the Bible, Abel was killed by his brother Cain, the first murder victim

explanation.surface: An author presents a murder victim in an elevator, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of the word for lift, and 'in' places the Biblical victim inside it. 'presenting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was a French Renaissance writer, author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Rosencrantz initially wearing Hamlet's shabby underwear

indicators.note: wearing means the anagrammed letters are put on around the first letter
shabby means worn and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its possessive s, all used as letters

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the name Rosencrantz

explanation.surface: Rosencrantz is first seen in the prince's tatty undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shabby' rearranges HAMLETS, and 'wearing' puts R, the first letter of 'Rosencrantz', inside it. The S of 'Hamlet's' counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermals are warm undergarments worn for insulation in cold weather.

clue.text: Upright individual's state

parts.note: an individual is one; the 's stands for 'is', a link
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota, a US state

explanation.surface: A single person's condition is described as upstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stood on end is vertical, so the phrase means upright.

clue.text: Bore outside local missing first drink

indicators.note: outside means the word for bore wraps around the shortened pub

parts.note: the bore of a gun barrel is its calibre

indicators.note: missing first means the opening letter of the word for local is dropped

parts.note: a local is a British name for one's neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: A tedious person stands outside the pub, which has lost its first drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing first' drops P from the pub, and 'outside' wraps the word for bore around what is left. 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but it means the width of a gun barrel; 'local' is British for a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuba libre is a cocktail of rum, cola and lime, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Time up for mountaineer disheartened by call

indicators.note: disheartened means the middle letter, the heart, of the climber's name is removed

parts.note: Sir Edmund Hillary was the mountaineer who first climbed Everest with Tenzing
to call something by a name is to term it

explanation.surface: A climber is dispirited by a summons that means his time is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes one central L out of HILLARY, leaving HILARY. Being 'up' means being in residence at Oxford or Cambridge university, and Hilary term is Oxford's spring term.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary term is a period of the academic year when students are up at Oxford.

clue.text: Mollusc left in river

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for left goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A shellfish has been abandoned in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like 'abandoned', but here it is just the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a bivalve shellfish, a kind of mollusc.

clue.text: Rome isn't so chaotic for a methodical Italian

indicators.note: chaotic means disordered, so these letters are put into a jumble

explanation.surface: Rome is less chaotic than people think, for an orderly Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaotic' rearranges ROME ISNT SO; 'for a' is a link. 'methodical' is the pun: Maria Montessori devised an educational method.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Montessori was an Italian educator famous for the teaching method named after her.

clue.text: Girl to get money abroad as member of volunteer force

parts.note: Terri is a girl's name
the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries, so foreign money

explanation.surface: A girl goes overseas to earn money as a part-time soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's reserve force of part-time volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Territorial is a soldier in Britain's Territorial Army, a reserve force of part-time volunteers.

clue.text: Socialist Worker admitting sailor is slowing down

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the sailor goes inside the socialist

parts.note: red is a common term for a socialist or communist
a tar is a sailor
the ant is the crossword's typical worker insect

explanation.surface: Socialist Worker lets in a sailor, which slows things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts the sailor inside the socialist. Socialist Worker is also the name of a British left-wing newspaper, which disguises the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A retardant substance delays or slows down a process such as burning.

clue.text: A great fellow entertaining any number in Oxfordshire

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the number is taken inside the other words

parts.note: great means big
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A distinguished academic hosts countless people at a place in Oxfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts N inside the great fellow, landing between the second and third letters. The definition names a place by where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Abingdon is a market town found in Oxfordshire, England.

clue.text: Top churchmen beginning to preach about differences

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word preach

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a topic
tiffs are petty quarrels, differences of opinion

explanation.surface: Senior clergymen begin to preach about their disagreements.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiffs are popes or high bishops, the senior figures of the church.

clue.text: Capital station no longer in boulevard regarded by Paul?

definitions.meaning: a London railway terminus in the City that closed in 1986
Paul McCartney's 1984 film and album was titled Give My Regards to the wide street named here

explanation.surface: A closed London station sits on an avenue that Paul thinks highly of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The second definition puns on 'regards': McCartney's film was Give My Regards to Broad Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad Street was a London terminus closed in 1986, and the street in McCartney's film title.

clue.text: Box outside youth centre for clergyman

indicators.note: outside means the box surrounds the central letter

parts.note: a crate is a box

indicators.note: centre means the middle letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: A box is placed outside a youth centre for the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes U, the middle of 'youth', and 'outside' puts the box round it. 'youth centre' looks like a youth club.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is a clergyman who assists a parish priest.

clue.text: Female goes out with Oscar to see saws

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name

indicators.note: out means the letter for Oscar is ejected from the word goes

parts.note: taken as written
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman goes out with a man called Oscar to look at some saws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes O from GOES to leave GES; 'with' and 'to see' are links. 'saws' looks like tools, but they are sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, so saws are adages.

clue.text: Bill or Mark

definitions.meaning: a banknote, a paper bill of money
a mark meaning a written jotting, a brief comment, or a distinguishing sign

explanation.definitionFit: A banknote is a bill, and to make a note of something is to mark it.

clue.text: Police car originally used by Frost taking first of suspects to court

indicators.note: originally means the opening letter of the word car is wanted

parts.note: rime is a white frost of ice crystals

indicators.note: first of means the first letter of the word suspects is taken

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard at a college

explanation.surface: A police car driven by Inspector Frost brings a suspect to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' suggests the TV detective Jack Frost, but it gives RIME. 'used by', 'taking' and 'to' are links. The definition 'Police' is the plural force.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime squad is a police unit that investigates serious offences.

clue.text: Lead, say, for Bond's boss and others

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 and James Bond's boss in the Fleming novels
et al is the Latin abbreviation for 'and others'

explanation.surface: James Bond's chief and others take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead, say' looks like a verb about leading, but it is lead the heavy element, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a metal, which the 'say' signals.

clue.text: Runner required by Spielberg

indicators.note: required by means the letters are contained within the director's name

explanation.surface: Spielberg needs a sprinter for his film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete or film runner, but a runner is crossword shorthand for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river runs, so it is a runner; the Elbe is a German river.

clue.text: Stripper often laid off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone bad or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer is frequently made redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges OFTEN LAID. 'Stripper' suggests a dancer, but it means a chemical that strips leaves from plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A defoliant strips plants of their leaves, so it is a stripper in a botanical sense.

clue.text: Insufficient fruit for ape

indicators.note: insufficient means the fruit falls short, missing its last letter

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: There isn't enough fruit to feed the ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insufficient' drops the last letter of ORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orang is a short form of orangutan, the red-haired great ape.

clue.text: Was 21 different? Don't worry about it!

indicators.note: different means the letters are made into something other than they were

parts.note: 21 points to the solution of 21 across, a word for a bill or mark

explanation.surface: Was the bill altered? Never mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges WAS plus NOTE, the answer to 21 across.
explanation.definitionFit: No sweat is an idiom meaning it's no trouble, so don't worry about it.

clue.text: Tories put out after Liberal leader waits around

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters come behind the Liberal's first letter
leader means the first letter of the word Liberal
put out means the word Tories is disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Conservatives are upset after the Liberal leader keeps them hanging around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges the letters of 'Tories', and 'after' puts that behind L, the first letter of 'Liberal'.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly, so someone who loiters waits around.
